before.title: 48V Mild Hybrid Battery Issues
before.description: The 48V EQ Boost mild hybrid system battery degrades or fails prematurely, triggering multiple warning messages and disabling the start-stop, electric boost, and regenerative braking functions. Software glitches also cause false battery fault warnings.
before.solution: Have the dealer diagnose with XENTRY to differentiate between a software fault and genuine battery failure. Update to the latest software calibration. If the 48V lithium-ion battery has failed, replacement runs $1,500-3,000 at the dealer.
symptoms: Multiple electrical warning messages on dashboard
Start-stop system disabled

citations.title: MBWorld.org - W223 S-Class 48V EQ Boost battery failures and software updates

communityRecommendations.content: Request the latest XENTRY software update before approving a battery replacement. Many 48V fault codes are resolved by software calibration alone.

proposal.title: 48V Mild Hybrid Battery Issues
proposal.description: Mercedes records establish multiple 48V-battery warning and charging conditions on 2021-2024 S-Class vehicles, but not a universal premature-failure rate. Communications 11012782 and 11013190 identify a false P0A7F00 aging calculation at cold battery temperatures and explicitly say not to replace parts before the software correction. Other records require state-of-health testing, charging-system diagnosis or campaign software before hardware selection.
proposal.solution: Preserve the exact 48V message and every fault code, then follow XENTRY tests for the 12V supply, 48V state of charge and health, battery-control software, integrated starter-alternator and powertrain software. Apply the VIN-specific campaign or software remedy first where applicable. Replace a 48V battery only after the Mercedes procedure confirms it; do not buy a battery from this page because part number, state of health and VIN fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: 48V or hybrid-system warning documented
battery state of charge and health measured
software and charging paths separated from confirmed hardware failure

before.title: ABC Hydraulic Suspension System Leak
before.description: The Active Body Control (ABC) hydraulic suspension system develops leaks in the struts, lines, tandem pump, and accumulators. Repairs are extremely expensive as the system operates at 3,000+ PSI. Leaks cause the car to sag and ride harshly.
before.solution: Locate and repair the leak. ABC struts are $1,000-2,500 each, the tandem pump is $1,500-3,000, and accumulators are $200-500 each. Some owners convert to conventional air or coil spring suspension to escape ABC costs.
symptoms: Vehicle sags on one corner
Warning message: "Stop vehicle, visit workshop"

citations.title: MBWorld.org - Complete ABC system failure guide and conversion to AIRMATIC/coilovers

communityRecommendations.content: Budget $2,000-5,000/year for ABC maintenance on a used S-Class. If the system is too expensive, a coil spring conversion runs $2,000-3,000 and eliminates all future ABC costs.

proposal.title: ABC Hydraulic Suspension System Leak
proposal.description: Mercedes records establish hydraulic leakage in the Active Body Control system on older S-Class platforms, but the failed component must be identified. Communication 10009985 covers a heat- and humidity-affected high-pressure distribution hose on certain twelve-cylinder vehicles; other records cover a pressure-supply valve-unit line, a high-pressure line, a pulsation damper sleeve and model-specific leak paths. They do not establish one universal strut, tandem-pump or accumulator failure across every stored year and trim.
proposal.solution: If an ABC warning, sag or hydraulic-fluid loss is present, stop if the vehicle cannot maintain safe ride height. Clean and inspect the system, preserve fault and pressure data, and locate the leak at the line, hose, valve unit, pulsation damper, strut or pump before authorizing repair. Use the VIN-specific Mercedes procedure and fluid specification. Do not buy an ABC line, strut, pump, accumulator or conversion kit from this page; the failed component and fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: ABC warning and ride height documented
hydraulic leak location identified
line, valve, damper, strut and pump paths separated

before.title: AIRMATIC Air Suspension Compressor Failure
before.description: The AIRMATIC air suspension compressor burns out from overwork, typically caused by slow leaks in the air springs that force the compressor to run excessively. Compressor failure leaves the vehicle sitting low with a harsh ride.
before.solution: Replace the air suspension compressor and relay. Inspect all four air springs for leaks before replacing the compressor — a new compressor will fail quickly if the underlying leak is not fixed. Arnott makes a quality aftermarket replacement.
symptoms: Vehicle sits very low after being parked
Compressor noise stops and car does not rise

citations.title: MBWorld.org - S-Class AIRMATIC compressor replacement and leak testing guide

communityRecommendations.content: Always fix air spring leaks before replacing the compressor. A leaking strut will burn out a new compressor within months.

proposal.title: AIRMATIC Air Suspension Compressor Failure
proposal.description: The reviewed S-Class corpus does not establish compressor burnout from leaking air springs across model years 2006-2020. Exact records identify separate front-strut leakage, drain-valve wiring faults, control-unit software, pressure-line checks, corrosion at a rear strut foot joint and model-specific AIRMATIC warnings. Those paths cannot be collapsed into one universal failed compressor.
proposal.solution: Document ride height, warning text, compressor operation and fault codes. Leak-test the struts, lines, valve unit and reservoir, then test compressor power, relay, drain-valve wiring, output and control software under the VIN-specific Mercedes procedure. Do not buy a compressor, relay, strut or air spring from this page; the failed path and fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: ride height and warning state documented
air leaks and pressure retention tested
compressor hardware, drain-valve wiring and software paths separated
affectedSystems: air struts, lines, valve unit and reservoir

before.solution: Replace or refurbish the COMAND head unit. Specialist companies can repair the internal components for $400-800 vs $3,000+ for a new OEM unit. Update to the latest map and firmware version after replacement.

No audio output from any source

communityRecommendations.content: Send your COMAND unit to a specialist for repair rather than buying new. Companies like BeckerAutoSound and CarRadioRepair fix them for a fraction of dealer cost.

before.title: Magic Body Control Camera Failure

before.solution: Recalibrate the Magic Body Control camera with XENTRY diagnostic tools. If the camera module has failed, replacement runs $1,000-2,000 plus calibration. A windshield replacement also requires recalibration.

Ride quality degrades to standard suspension mode

before.title: Power Steering Pump Leak
before.description: The power steering pump develops a leak at the shaft seal or high-pressure line fitting, causing fluid loss and a whining noise when turning. Low fluid levels can damage the steering rack and ABC system (if equipped).
before.solution: Replace the power steering pump seal or the entire pump if internally worn. Flush the power steering system with fresh CHF 11S fluid. Inspect the high-pressure hose for leaks.
symptoms: Whining noise when turning the steering wheel
Power steering fluid puddle under the car

citations.title: BenzWorld.org - W220 S-Class power steering pump replacement guide

communityRecommendations.content: Use only CHF 11S (Pentosin) power steering fluid in Mercedes vehicles. ATF will damage the seals and rack. This is the number one mistake made by quick-lube shops.

proposal.title: Power Steering Pump Leak
proposal.description: The reviewed corpus does not establish a recurring power-steering-pump shaft-seal failure across model years 2000-2010. Exact records identify hydraulic-line-fitting leakage on a limited 2000-2001 population, high-pressure-line routing on a 2007 S550 4MATIC, a 2010 steering-pump whine, and later electrohydraulic pump or electric-steering conditions. These do not prove the stored shaft-seal mechanism or universal fluid and repair prescription.
proposal.solution: Document fluid level and specification, leak location, steering effort and noise. Clean the system and inspect reservoir, damper and pressure/return lines, fittings, pump and rack separately, then follow the VIN-specific Mercedes procedure. Do not buy a pump, seal, hose, rack or fluid from this page; the leak source, fluid specification and fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: fluid loss and leak source documented
steering effort and noise reproduced
line, fitting, pump and rack paths separated
